extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: A benchmark of 11.5K multimodal questions spanning 6 disciplines, 30 subjects, and 183 subfields, curated from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials to evaluate multimodal understanding and reasoning at college level.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was collected in three stages: first, the authors selected 30 subjects from six disciplines based on common university majors and the presence of visual inputs; second, over 50 university students, including co-authors, collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources and created new questions where necessary; third, the authors cleaned the data by removing duplicates, checking format and typos, and assigning difficulty levels, excluding about 10% of very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Potential duplicates were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, then reviewed and removed by authors; problems were checked for format and typos; questions were categorized into four difficulty levels, and approximately 10% of very easy problems were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal, format and typo checking, difficulty categorization, and exclusion of very easy problems not matching design criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students specializing in the selected majors collected multimodal questions and created new questions when necessary. Annotators were instructed to follow copyright and license regulations, avoid sources prohibiting copying or redistribution, and select questions without immediately available answers. The detailed annotation protocol is described in the appendix.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification was developed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A secondary review team vetted annotations; regular audits of random samples were conducted; ambiguities were flagged for collaborative review; error analysis on GPT-4V predictions was performed by expert annotators using golden explanations when available.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the relevant majors; 90 college senior students were used as human experts for validation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Version change log provided with updates from V1 to V4, including added model results, corrected typos, updated names, and added human expert results; the live-updating leaderboard is available on the project website.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The protocol states that annotators should avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to monitor progress toward Expert AGI and may help develop next-generation multimodal foundation models; the paper notes potential risks of job displacement and economic disruption if Expert AGI is achieved.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping between MMMU performance and the 90th percentile of skilled adults, and college exams are not the only tasks an AGI should tackle. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects may be insufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, evaluation, validation, and zero-shot testing of multimodal models; the dataset is divided into development, validation, and test sets, and the validation set is used for hyperparameter selection.
